### Send a GET request with HTTPX

Source: https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/0.27.2/README.md

Demonstrates sending a basic synchronous GET request and inspecting the response object, status code, headers, and text content.

```pycon
>>> import httpx
>>> r = httpx.get('https://www.example.org/')
>>> r
<Response [200 OK]>
>>> r.status_code
200
>>> r.headers['content-type']
'text/html; charset=UTF-8'
>>> r.text
'<!doctype html>\n<html>\n<head>\n<title>Example Domain</title>...'
```

I added a `status` command to `tools/cli.py`, but I haven't run it. My test command needed approval and was blocked. The code is written against the httpx 0.27.2 docs from Context7, which match the version pinned in the Dockerfile.

Usage:

```
python tools/cli.py status https://example.com https://httpbin.org/status/404
# 200 https://example.com
# 404 https://httpbin.org/status/404
```

- **Output:** one line per URL, in the form `<code> <url>`.
- **Redirects:** they aren't followed by default, so you'll see the 301 or 302. Pass `--follow-redirects` to get the final status instead.
- **Timeout:** `--timeout` sets the per-request timeout in seconds (default 10).
- **Errors:** a URL that can't be reached (DNS failure, timeout and so on) prints `ERR <url> (<reason>)` and the run continues. The command exits with code 1 if any URL failed this way.
- **Docker:** it works through the existing entrypoint, e.g. `docker run <image> status https://example.com`. No Dockerfile changes were needed.

To check it, run `python3 tools/cli.py status --help`, or build the image and try a couple of URLs. If you approve it, I'll run the check myself.
